- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts often overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-90+ levels), then gradually correct downward — model fails to capture this deceleration.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds high forecasts longer than actual price tends to revert toward recent lower or medium-range levels.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in the first 10–15 days; later days show better alignment with true values, suggesting model adjusts as new data arrives.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often continues to forecast higher than true price after a sharp decline.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short-term (1–3 days) and overly pessimistic in the medium-term (7–15 days) — model may be misweighting volatility vs. trend.
